author: Doctor
text:
Another quick follow up.

Here is a 30min chart and the blue lines have changed from their previous green because it was not very clear for support and resistance outlining the price range formed by today's price action.

Note 'A' which points to the most recent demand where buyers came in with good strength, the second test after this on B shows they bulls still want more orders and the bears and also not interested in taking this lower.

Here is a 5min chart, within the shaded area is compression. This price action is meant to take all the sellers along with price as it moves. But we have failed to see it go further than the 30min demand/support and this still gives a stronger hand to the bulls even though we dont see solid price action higher up to see this.

NY close coming up in 20 mins and while the forex wont close, we may get a poke above the price range it will really help the bulls. At this point in time our bullish support is weakening and we need all the help we get and some NY closing noise would be great.

Also note the demand reaction on the 5min out of this area in the past. Against us is market timing.

So?.....we wait and we wait.

author: Doctor
text: Now we see clear buying coming in and 5min supply getting ignored. All good for the bulls. If supply was taken along for the ride in a compression play, it makes it easier for the bulls later because all the sellers are gone. This is not set in stone, but it tends to play out like this very often.

author: Doctor
text:
hornet, on your last chart you you have two red lines on top, these when combined is a stacked area of supply, the lines on their own mean less.

On the lowest blue line you can see price comeback and touch it and see support. This is common place and I take trades off these all the time. But if you draw another line at the very bottom of price on that chart, the area then between your new bottom line and the line I just mentioned where support comes in, now becomes you area of demand. A line on its own wont concentrate your eye enough, all it does it make you focus far too tight into one price.

to, yes I know, each to his own and there was a time many moons ago I used trend lines, channels etc. Given the bulls failed, we now wait to see what kind of reaction we get from over head near term resistance. A short move down into the last 4hr demand would be enough to make me take it. I would not load up on this as it is still counter trend.

At the moment we are slowly coming down into an area where we saw strong demand. However the bulls buying in there will have a hard time trying to get up through the last few days price action. Only if enough orders come in would they run with it. My longer term bias is still bullish until I see major S/R broken. tested, and failure.

author: Doctor
text:
On lower time frames I still use 4hr+ as my guide. Even though I am now out of the euro trade I will still consider scaling in long. The higher time frames are still bullish and helping now is the lower time frame action showing bullish activity too. I will pull the trigger when it looks good to my eye.

Look for multiple reasons to take any trade, all must be obvious and pro money must show signs of activity for lower time frame entries to work.

The time frame you choose to enter must gel with your risk appetite and capital. Also be aware that when trading intraday you do not have the luxury of time. That is, waiting for a 1hr candle can miss out on a lot of trade entries. You have to decide what kind of move you want i.e how many points. Using a 1hr will net you more per trade, but you wont get many of those in a day. Where the 1hr candle shines (pun) is when it closes nicely at a good time during the trading day and there is resistance or support along with it. If price action on the 5 and 15min look good, then I will take it and know before hand if I am playing it to the next supply or demand area or if I will close some at that area and leave a portion on to run.

Where you place your entries, exits and how you manage the trades is a personal thing and there is no right or wrong, it is done to suit your pocket and style as a trader. Try developing a trading style on a time frame you feel comfortable with and take it from there. It will evolve over time into something that feels comfortable, and once you reach that, stop changing it and hone it down to become second nature. It may not be there yet, but when you see the right setup for your style, light bulbs go off and you are all set.

Screen time is the best educator there is.
